notes: visual-qa-log.json (2026-10-18) verdict=issues, ONE medium finding: at 375px the Juventus crest on the 'Lazio at Juventus' Serie A row is described as 'a plain outlined box (browser's default broken-image placeholder), not a club crest', apparently a missing/broken image asset specific to Juventus. No high findings; no other medium.

Investigated the asset path end to end: docs/logos/juventus.png EXISTS and is a valid 96x96 RGBA PNG (byte-format identical to the crests that render fine). entities.json carries logo.file='juventus.png', basis='editorial-use', source='espn', so ssEntityLogoSrc() resolves to 'logos/juventus.png' and the is emitted normally. The image is NOT failing to load / 404 — it decodes.

Pixel analysis via Chromium canvas settles it: juventus.png is all-black line art on a transparent background — avgLum 3.2, maxLum 114, 0% light pixels, 0% coloured — versus working crests (ac-milan avgLum 93.8 / maxLum 255 / 16% coloured; arsenal 55% coloured). So it renders EFFECTIVELY INVISIBLE against the true-black dark theme (#000000 page, #1C1C1E cell); the vision model read that faint near-invisible shape as an outlined/broken-image box. This is the SAME underlying issue the 2026-10-12/14/16 visual-qa runs described as an 'invisible box' and the 2026-10-17 ui-fix run abandoned — redescribed, not a new failed-load bug.

Tested the one plausible in-scope code fix and rejected it: a load-failure fallback (adding onerror to the logo to drop a broken mark) is a NO-OP here because the image loads successfully, so onerror never fires and the invisible black crest persists. Verified with a Chromium harness rendering the real entity-avatar.js: a working asset keeps its , a 404 src collapses cleanly under onerror, but Juventus is the working-asset case. Shipping onerror would falsely close this finding while the live site still shows an invisible crest, so I discarded it (git checkout).

No licensing-compliant CSS/JS fix exists within this loop's scope. WP-186 + DESIGN.md Entitets-avatar trinn 0 require every club mark shown UNMODIFIED — explicitly no filter, tint, mix-blend-mode, border-radius clipping, background plate, or drop-shadow (a CC BY-SA mark may not be made a derivative, and visual-qa itself warned the loop not to silently patch this with a background plate). Every technique that would make black-on-transparent visible against black is exactly what that normative contract forbids, and this PR would auto-merge to the live site.

The genuine fixes are out of this loop's touch-set (docs/index.html, docs/css/**, docs/js/** only): (a) replace juventus.png in docs/logos/** with a crest carrying a light/coloured element — an asset + licensing decision for build-entities / the logo seeder, not the frontend; or (b) a human-weighed WP-186 policy change, e.g. fall back to the colour monogram ('JU' on Juventus's #000000/#e8a2b0 split, which IS visible) for effectively-monochrome-dark marks, or a sanctioned hairline/plate deviation. Both require explicit owner instruction per DESIGN.md.

Nothing load-bearing is lost — the team-name text still identifies the match. Abandoning rather than shipping a no-op or a licensing-violating change to the live site; leaving for human/owner judgment (an asset swap or a WP-186 policy call).
